correctness.rationale: At every observed prefix, all possible accepted spans come from a finite subset-span family. The intersection-dimension signature with that family determines every acceptance-LP subspace constraint, leaving finitely many essential constraints over an arbitrary field. The motivating paper's finite-signature modular uncrossing and fixed-chain feasibility argument then applies, and the remainder of its 1/e online analysis is field-independent.

originality.rationale: The motivating paper explicitly restricts its online-representation theorem to finite fields, while its arbitrary-field argument applies only when the full finite matroid is known in advance. It separately develops finite signatures for infinitely many flats. Searches found no inspected source combining these ingredients to give the arbitrary-field online-representation theorem or the fixed finite-rank modular-ambient online formulation. Originality is only to the best of our knowledge, with unusually high near-simultaneous-work risk.

value.rationale: The result removes a substantive information-model restriction from a major new strong-secretary theorem, extending online vector streams to arbitrary fields such as Q, R, and C and isolating finite-rank modular ambient geometry as the structural requirement rather than field finiteness.
